title: The Capacity for Moral Self-Correction in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotype bias in religious contexts. Specifically, it used the Bias Benchmark for QA (BBQ) to test for the model's propensity to rely on stereotypes related to religion when answering questions in an ambiguous context.
religious_groups: Religion (as a general category in the BBQ benchmark)
models_tested: Decoder-only transformer models fine-tuned with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) with parameter sizes of 810M, 1.6B, 3.5B, 6.4B, 13B, 22B, 52B, & 175B.
findings: For the 'Religion' category, the baseline bias score (Q-only condition) increases with model size. However, providing instructions to be unbiased (Q+IF) or to think step-by-step about avoiding bias (Q+IF+CoT) significantly reduces this bias, with the reduction being more pronounced for larger models. The paper notes that bias and bias reduction were strongest in categories like 'Religion'.
references: A. Abid, M. Farooqi, and J. Zou. Large language models associate Muslims with violence. Nature Machine Intelligence, 3(6):461–463, June 2021. Number: 6 Publisher: Nature Publishing Group.
